title: Investigation of Atomic Structure and Oxygen Sublattice in La3Ni2O7 Single Crystals
content: Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) and infinite-layer nickelates have emerged as promising candidates for high-temperature superconductivity. Both structures are derivatives of the ABO3 perovskite aristotype. In an infinite-layer nickelate, ANiO2, the apical oxygen atoms are removed from the NiO6 octahedra, resulting in the square-planar coordination of Ni in NiO2 layers [1, 2]. Meanwhile, for RP nickelates, Lan+1NinO3n+1, the structure is derived from the disruption of the perovskite framework with the insertion of double rocksalt layers. In our previous work, we reported the discovery of a novel long-range coherent polymorphism in La3Ni2O7 single crystals [3]. Instead of a uniform bilayer stacking of NiO6 octahedra (La3Ni2O7-2222 phase), we observed a unique stacking sequence of alternating single-layer and trilayer blocks of NiO6, resulting in a La3Ni2O7-1313 phase. The structure and properties of RP nickelates are highly correlated. For Lan+1NinO3n+1, depending on the structural motif (n = 1, 2, 3…) and the stacking sequence, these single crystals could yield insulating, charge-spin ordering, metallic, and high-temperature superconducting states. For instance, La3Ni2O7-2222 single crystals have shown superconductivity up to a temperature of 80 K between a pressure range of 14 to 43.5 GPa [4]. Moreover, oxygen sub-stoichiometry because of heterogeneous reduction in thin film infinite-layer nickelates [2], and variable oxygen pressure during La3Ni2O7-δ single crystals synthesis is prevalent but is not well quantified and understood. Therefore, to exploit novel functionalities in these nickelates, it is critical to understand the role of atomic structure and oxygen sub-stoichiometry on the electronic structure of these nickelates.
